input_kinds.label: OBSERVED
input_kinds.definition: Direct observation recorded for the bounded study or test.

input_kinds.label: ACQUIRED
input_kinds.definition: Existing real-world data obtained from a declared external source.

input_kinds.label: DERIVED
input_kinds.definition: Produced from other records through a declared transformation.

input_kinds.label: SIMULATED
input_kinds.definition: Produced by a model under stated assumptions or conditions.

input_kinds.label: REPORTED
input_kinds.definition: Supplied as a report or assertion rather than directly observed by the project.

input_kinds.label: UNESTABLISHED

substantiation.label: SOURCE-STATED

research.title: HATI-Madrid — Heat-Adaptive Tourism Opportunity Screening (Madrid pilot)
research.summary: Published preprint testing whether the choice of thermal representation changes heat-adaptive tourism screening decisions.
research.research_question: Does physically based (SOLWEIG/UTCI) thermal modelling materially alter tourism-feasibility classifications relative to the simple air-temperature-and-tree-presence proxy, and is any difference physically interpretable?
research.research_question_note: RQ1, verbatim (preprint §1). RQ2 addresses decision-support value; RQ3 robustness and traceability.

summary: A single-city, single-day pilot of a constraint-first, uncertainty-aware screening architecture.
Study area: the Prado–Retiro–Atocha box (≈3.5 km²); 27 tourism assets curated from OpenStreetMap (13 indoor, 14 outdoor) — a purposive selection, not a representative sample.
Time: 21 August 2023, inside an AEMET-designated extreme-heat episode (20–25 August 2023), at 12:00, 15:00 and 18:00 CEST.

Two thermal representations — an operational proxy (ambient air-temperature hazard band plus nearby tree presence) and SOLWEIG → Tmrt → UTCI — feed one ordered gate chain: open? → reachable? → thermally feasible? → evidence sufficient? → meaningful improvement?
Compared with a nearest-open baseline over eight pre-registered decision scenarios.

code.note: src/, tests/ and app/ only, since 2026-11-11

data.note: Third-party data keeps its licences; derived outputs "all rights reserved".

text.note: The deposited preprint; repository documents are not_stated.

reproducibility.note: Code, outputs and REPRODUCIBILITY.md are public; the Atlas did not re-run them.

research.verification_note: Checked against the deposited preprint: abstract, §1 research questions, §2.1, licence statement (p. 18) and Figure 1–4 captions. No other part of the full text was verified.

research.title: HATI — Pedestrian Heat Extension
research.summary: Frozen robustness case for evidence-first pedestrian heat comparison.
research.research_question: Across the two frozen Atocha–Puerta de Alcalá routes and tested departure times, does the modelled thermal evidence remain strong enough under justified canopy-vintage and side-of-street perturbations to establish either route as robustly cooler?

summary: Modelled comparison of two frozen, hashed routes for OD1 (Atocha → Puerta de Alcalá): Route A, the Paseo del Prado / Recoletos axis (2,657.8 m); Route B, the Alfonso XII park-edge (2,365.7 m).
Frozen study day 2023-08-24, departures 14:00 and 17:00.
Thermal model: stateful single-call SOLWEIG producing UTCI, as a continuous 72-step, 15-minute sequence.
Five frozen perturbations, including canopy source and vintage, and side-of-street; pre-registered negative controls.
Frozen decision rule: a sign reversal under a justified perturbation, or an ensemble spanning zero, yields ABSTAIN.

code.note: None at the pin; MIT added for src/, tests/ and app/ on 2026-11-11, after the pin.

data.note: Route geometry is OpenStreetMap-derived (ODbL 1.0); other derived data not_stated.

reproducibility.note: Frozen inputs, hashes and the perturbation results CSV are committed; the Atlas did not re-run them.

research.title: SNTO — PNSG Decision Evidence
research.summary: Bounded destination-management case using environmental and governance evidence.
research.research_question: With the evidence currently ingested, which PNSG public-use units, if any, justify priority management review or monitoring for the 2027 planning cycle, and where is evidence insufficient to establish priority?
research.research_question_note: Carried forward unchanged from v0.2; matches the brief §1 decision question.

summary: Monthly Sentinel-2 (S2_SR_HARMONIZED) NDVI, NDMI and EVI for 21 PNSG campaign assets, 2021-01 to 2026-06 (66 months).
Trend tests: Mann-Kendall on the deseasonalised series with tie correction; Sen slope with a non-parametric confidence interval; Yue-Pilon pre-whitening robustness check.
Combined with official PRUG zoning and a two-scene ΔEHS reading of 218 OAPN trails.
Governing rules: a claim may not be finer than its evidence; environmental change is not tourism impact; each unit receives a decision status (priority / monitor / insufficient).

code.note: Academic and research use; commercial use needs written permission. The Zenodo software record states CC BY 4.0 — an unresolved discrepancy (Q4). Public source availability is not an open-source licence.

reproducibility.note: The time series and Mann-Kendall results are committed; the Atlas did not re-run them.

research.title: Pedestrian Network Accessibility Pilot (San Isidro, Madrid)
research.summary: Isolated, bounded experiment measuring how far straight-line distance departs from pedestrian-network distance to municipal sports facilities.
research.research_question: For official address portals in one Madrid barrio, how far does the straight-line distance to the nearest official municipal basic sports facility depart from the shortest distance along the OpenStreetMap pedestrian network, and does the choice of metric change which facility is nearest?
research.research_question_note: Verbatim from the pilot README (the source's bold emphasis removed).
research.lifecycle_note: Verdict issued; follow-up audit closed with HOLD.

summary: Origins: 2,651 official address portals (TIPO_NDP = PORTAL, callejero 213605) in barrio 113.
Destinations: 38 access points of municipal basic sports facilities (dataset 200215) within 1,000 m of the barrio.
Network: an OpenStreetMap pedestrian graph from an Overpass extract (the barrio plus 1,600 m), 16,715 ways retained.
Measurement in EPSG:25830: for each origin, the nearest facility by straight line and by shortest network path; four quantities — detour ratio, understatement, discordance and false inclusion.
Four acceptance criteria (A1–A4), documented retrospectively and stated by the source as not pre-registered; seven sensitivity variants.

data.note: Ayuntamiento de Madrid data CC BY 4.0; the OSM extract and derived network values ODbL 1.0.

reproducibility.note: Pipeline, tests and query are public and the OSM extract is archived; municipal inputs are mutable at source. The follow-up audit reproduced the input selection, not a byte-identical rerun. The Atlas did not re-run it.

research.title: Madrid Urban Evidence Lens
research.summary: A place-first, static web application for reading what official sources document about urban development in Madrid, and what that evidence does not let you conclude.
research.documents: Descriptive counts and official context for a chosen place in Madrid — barrio, registered residents, licensed tourist dwellings (VUT), registered unemployment and planning ámbito — plus place-to-place comparison and city-level INE hotel-demand context. Each source carries provenance, licence and an interpretation ceiling.
research.claim_limits: It does not establish tourist pressure, carrying capacity, tourist behaviour or footfall, safety outcomes, tourism quality, rankings or composite scores, economic impact, causal effects of heat, real-time conditions, or city-wide heat coverage.
research.hosts_note: Hosted as an isolated research package; the source states that nothing in the application references it.

research.title: SNTO — Smart Nature Tourism Observatory
research.summary: Public research observatory turning Sentinel-2 and official OAPN cartography into environmental-change evidence for protected-area public-use management, with explicit limits on tourism attribution. Its source code is publicly available under a custom academic-use licence, which is not an open-source licence.
research.documents: Pipeline A: real Sentinel-2 indicators for the PNSG, including the 21-asset 2021–2026 trend layer and 218 OAPN trails, with official PRUG zoning. Pipeline B: a governance demonstration on 20 synthetic assets.
research.claim_limits: Field validation (#26) has not run; the three v2.2 real-data paths (MITMA mobility, SCM zones, SVI series) are built but not ingested; the economic layer consists of conditional scenarios; there is no causal attribution of change to tourism. The causal rationale in the README (trampling → compaction → spectral signal) is a design hypothesis of the platform and is not presented here as an established finding.

code.note: Academic and research use. The Zenodo record states CC BY 4.0 — discrepancy preserved (Q4).

research.title: Madrid Transit Graph — Metro de Madrid topology and disruption studies
research.summary: Reproducible topological graph of the Metro de Madrid network from OpenStreetMap, with pre-registered structural disruption studies that remain NEEDS_VALIDATION.
research.research_question: Which stations, when (a) their interchange function is disabled or (b) the station is closed, produce the largest increase in planned (scheduled) shortest travel time over all ordered station pairs, by time band? Is that ranking explained by simple structural metrics (degree, line count, betweenness)?
research.research_question_note: Verbatim from the v0.5 pre-registration §1 (the source's bold emphasis removed). Earlier studies (v0.2–v0.4) asked related structural questions on the same frozen v0.1.0 graph.

summary: Graph: Metro de Madrid lines L1–L12 and Ramal built with City2Graph 1.1.0 from an OpenStreetMap Overpass snapshot (OSM state 2026-11-19T18:17:06Z); node = aggregated station, edge = undirected pair of consecutive stations on at least one line.
Station merging is derived, not an OSM fact: stops with the same normalised name within 300 m are merged, then audited against CRTM open data (interchanges only).

v0.4: fragmentation under complete station removal. v0.5: planned travel times (segment length ÷ a speed per line, Line 3 imputed, waits and transfers assumed) under station closure or disabled interchange, by time band, against degree, line count and betweenness, with a pre-registration committed before the run.
The v0.1.0 snapshot is frozen and hash-checked; it cannot be re-derived exactly because the raw Overpass responses were not kept.

data.note: OpenStreetMap data in data/; CRTM-derived timing data are not distributed.

reproducibility.note: The frozen snapshot, pipeline, pre-registration and CI are public; regenerating is not reproducing the snapshot. The Atlas did not re-run it.

research.title: Madrid Isovist Demo — 2D isovists in Lavapiés and the Step 0 redundancy screen
research.summary: Closed exploratory pilot that computes 2D isovists from building footprints in Lavapiés and tested, with a pre-hashed stopping rule, whether they add anything to built density and the street network.
research.research_question: ¿una isovista 2D de huellas añade algo a la densidad edificada y a la red de calles?
research.research_question_note: Verbatim from the README (Step 0). English translation by the Atlas: does a 2D footprint isovist add anything to built density and the street network?

summary: Isovist: 360 rays plus one ray per vertex, obstacles = roof footprints, 100 m maximum radius by default; recomputed in the browser and checked against the Python implementation.
Step 0: 250 points every 20 m on the EMT pedestrian axes of the central 400 m, spatial block cross-validation with 100 m blocks.
Controls: built density, distance to footprint, street width, network position, and OpenStreetMap points of interest and stops (ODbL).
Stopping rule fixed and recorded with a hash before computing: an isovist measure is redundant when the controls reach validated R² ≥ 0.85.

data.note: Ayuntamiento de Madrid footprints under its general reuse conditions; OpenStreetMap under ODbL.

reproducibility.note: Code, tests and data notes are public; the Atlas did not re-run them.

research.verification_note: Spanish-language sources. Quotations are verbatim; translations are the Atlas's and are marked as such.

research.title: PNOA-LiDAR Madrid pilot — urban morphology in Embajadores (3rd coverage)
research.summary: Isolated research package, hosted in the Lens repository, testing what PNOA-LiDAR 3rd-coverage surface and terrain models add about urban morphology in one Madrid barrio.
research.research_question: What territorial evidence does PNOA-LiDAR (3rd coverage) add about urban morphology in Madrid, beyond what Madrid Urban Evidence Lens already uses?
research.lifecycle_note: Research line kept (MODIFY); revisit when IGN v2 or normalised building models are published (forecast 1H 2027) and an independent check exists.

summary: One MTN sheet (0559-4-5), MDS and MDT at 0.5 m from the PNOA-LiDAR 3rd coverage v1, downloaded by a person from the CNIG and identified by SHA-256.
Area of interest: the official polygon of barrio 012 Embajadores (1.034 km²).
Five acceptance criteria stated before the run (CRS, grid identity, valid cells, plausible terrain, negative differences), then MDS − MDT statistics inside the area.
A second run produced a byte-identical report and figure from the same inputs.

data.note: Results are derived works of IGN MDS/MDT 50 cm 3rd coverage; the rasters are not committed.

reproducibility.note: Pipeline and tests are public; the inputs need a manual CNIG download (reCAPTCHA). The Atlas did not re-run it.

research.title: Madrid Evidence MCP
research.summary: Local, read-only stdio MCP server that forwards a fixed set of query shapes to the Lens registry over pinned, hash-verified Lens files. It integrates no LLM and is not hosted.
research.lifecycle_note: Engineering prototype, not independently validated, not hosted.
research.territory_note: No case-specific territory: it answers point and circle queries over the Lens's Madrid data.

summary: Stage 2 evaluation: 6 new adversarial cases × 2 repetitions on the unchanged MCP v0.4, single arm, pre-registered at commit 61a74d6 before any run.
Runs were packaged blind and read by a language-model reader, not a human (readerIsHuman: false).
Pre-registered rule: 0 critical errors and 0 unsupported local claims → GO; E5/E6 or unsupported claims → MODIFY; E1/E2/E9 or technical failure → HOLD.

code.note: No licence file in the repository. Referenced only; no code or content is copied (decision E1).

data.note: Answers are the Lens's committed artifacts and carry the Lens's licences.

reproducibility.note: Server, tests and evaluation traces are public; running them needs a Lens checkout at commit f67cd47. The Atlas did not run them.

research.verification_note: The evaluation report is in Spanish; quotations are verbatim and translations are the Atlas's.

findings.statement: Changing the thermal representation reclassified one third of outdoor asset-time observations (33.3 %, 14 of 42), in both directions: in 9 the physical model was more restrictive, in 5 less restrictive.
findings.uncertainty: Reclassification differs by hour: 64.3 % at 12:00, 0.0 % at 15:00, 35.7 % at 18:00. Neither method is field-validated, so the direction of divergence says nothing about correctness.

findings.statement: Relative to the nearest-open baseline, constraint-first screening changed the feasible-alternative set in 7 of 8 scenarios. The nearest-open option failed screening in 3 of 8, and one scenario (S8) returned an explicit no-defensible-alternative outcome.

Under the tested uncertainty, 35 of 42 outdoor decisions were classed ROBUST, 6 BOUNDARY and 1 UNSTABLE. A satellite-derived irradiance realization changed 1 of 42 decisions; −10 % and −20 % irradiance perturbations changed none.
findings.uncertainty: Robustness covers only the tested dimensions (solar forcing, plus targeted canopy geometry for two assets). It is not total uncertainty and not a validation of the modelled field.

findings.statement: Baseline Route A − Route B mean-UTCI difference is 0.05 °C at 14:00 and 0.37 °C at 17:00.
findings.uncertainty: The perturbation ensemble spans zero at both times: −1.31…+0.23 °C (14:00) and −0.39…+0.38 °C (17:00).

findings.statement: The A−B sign reverses under the canopy perturbation (E-P2) at 14:00 and under side-of-street (E-P5) at 14:00 and 17:00.
Legitimate metrics disagree. Thermal intensity marginally favours A; exposure duration favours B (shorter route, fewer high-stress minutes).
Route point-max UTCI lies at 45.0–45.9 °C, next to the +46 °C extreme category boundary, across perturbations.
Of 21 assets with a real time series, 6 show significant greening, 14 no trend and 1 significant decline. The dominant signal is stability or recovery.

Maliciosa-Porrones (climbing area) shows a significant NDVI decline (τ = −0.37, p ≈ 0, n = 65; change-point 2025-03), but NDMI rises significantly (τ = +0.22, p = 0.01). The signals are internally contradictory. Status: MONITOR / DATA GAP.
findings.uncertainty: Evidence confidence LOW–MODERATE: strong temporal signal, poor spatial fit, no attribution evidence.

findings.statement: Zero units qualify for priority management review on public-use grounds. Across the 218 trails, the two-scene ΔEHS gives 165 improving and 46 worsening.
findings.uncertainty: Trail aggregate: MODERATE, because there is no visitor denominator and the reading is two-scene, not a time series.

findings.statement: Over 2,636 measured portals, the median detour ratio (same origin, same facility) is 1.354, and the mean is 1.538 over 2,634 pairs. The median understatement is 98.1 m.
findings.uncertainty: Medians across the sensitivity variants range from 1.347 to 1.922 (A4 passes in every variant). The denominator rule moves the median by 0.0008.

findings.statement: For 21.05 % of measured portals (555 of 2,636), the straight-line-nearest facility is not the network-nearest.
A "within X m" claim made on straight-line distance fails for 35.35 % of straight-line-inside portals at 300 m (614 of 1,737) and for 19.59 % at 500 m (465 of 2,374).

The follow-up audit of the municipal 500 m sports-proximity indicator concluded "HOLD para la comparación municipal" (2026-11-20). The indicator's executed calculation, inventory, population denominator and reference value were not located.
In v0.4, 84 of 242 complete station closures fragment the network; the public explorer layer reproduces this count exactly.
Planned times rank closures almost as hop counts do (ρ 0.956), and time bands change nothing (ρ ≥ 0.999).
findings.uncertainty: The pre-registered verdict depends on a metric that ignores disconnected pairs (source's own post-hoc check).

findings.statement: Built-form controls explain the mean isovist radius above the stopping threshold (validated R² 0.937) but not openness (0.833 against 0.85).
findings.uncertainty: 95 % intervals 0.904–0.951 (radius) and 0.762–0.874 (openness); over 30 repeated partitions openness never reached 0.85 (maximum 0.83) and radius always exceeded it.

findings.statement: The browser computation matches the Python implementation to within 0.5 % of area and 0.07 m of mean radius at the nine observers.
findings.uncertainty: The browser obstacle margin is an approximation, differing by up to 4.0 percentage points of area at +1.0 m.

findings.statement: Inside the barrio, the surface height above interpolated ground (MDS − MDT) has median 15.56 m and mean 13.65 m; 63.7 % of cells are at or above 12 m.
findings.uncertainty: Not building height: trees, vehicles, awnings and v1 misclassification are included.

findings.statement: Under the adopted reading of error E1 the pre-registered rule gives MODIFY; under the alternative reading two runs become critical errors and the rule gives HOLD.
findings.uncertainty: Unsupported local claims 1/12, Wilson 95 % interval 1.49 %–35.39 %; critical errors 0/12, interval 0 %–24.25 %.

outcomes.verdict_label: thermal representation is a substantive modelling choice in heat-adaptive tourism decision support
outcomes.statement: The findings indicate that thermal representation is a substantive modelling choice, and that a constraint-first architecture can expose that sensitivity while keeping uncertainty, evidence and exclusion logic explicit.
outcomes.claim_ceiling: The study evaluates decision sensitivity to the choice of thermal method, not the accuracy of either method against ground truth. Results are limited to a single Madrid pilot, without direct field validation of Tmrt/UTCI or observed tourist behaviour. The preprint is not peer-reviewed.
limitations: Single city.
Single day.
No field validation.
No behavioural data.

outcomes.statement: The route-difference sign reversed under at least one justified perturbation at both tested departure times and the ensemble spanned zero.
outcomes.claim_ceiling: Neither route is established as cooler, preferred, accurate, comfortable, behaviourally superior, physiologically safer, lower-dose, or healthier; the result does not mean the routes are thermally identical.
limitations: One OD pair, one day, two departures.
Modelled exposure only.
The verdict would change only with independent pedestrian-level Tmrt/UTCI measurement, an authoritative current canopy model, or resolved side-of-street mapping.

outcomes.statement: Evidence is insufficient to prioritise any physical intervention, closure, quota, restoration, or budget commitment; monitoring and improved data collection are the proportionate actions.
outcomes.claim_ceiling: No asset/trail visitor volume, tourism causality, ground condition, ecological impact, monetary allocation, closure, or restriction claim is supported.
limitations: No field validation by the author.
No causal attribution.
No visitor-use denominator.
Point and linestring footprints are a coarse proxy.

outcomes.statement: The experiment is defensible: all four documented criteria pass and the finding survives every valid variant. It does not license a product feature until five conditions are met: an OSM completeness audit; replication across contrasting barrios; a facility-register source gate; a qualified ODbL review; and a runtime decision.
outcomes.claim_ceiling: A single-barrio figure must never be shown as a Madrid figure. The result is a measured modelled-distance discrepancy, not an accessibility, equity or service-coverage assessment. The criteria were documented retrospectively, not pre-registered. No comparison with the municipal indicator is established (HOLD).
limitations: One barrio.
One facility category.
OSM completeness unaudited.
The ODbL status of derived outputs is contested and unresolved by the source.

outcomes.statement: One owner-attested iPhone field workflow passed the executed offline capture-to-backup checks with no intended data loss reported.
outcomes.claim_ceiling: FieldOS is not thereby validated, production-ready, field-proven across conditions, independently audited, or cross-platform verified.

outcomes.statement: The owner froze the research claim on 2026-11-21 and kept the repository as a documented demonstrator. Studies v0.2–v0.5 remain NEEDS_VALIDATION; no new analyses will be added unless an external validation source or a new, pre-registered question appears.
outcomes.claim_ceiling: No vulnerability or resilience result is claimed. Topological connectivity is not effective accessibility, operation, demand or observed resilience, and the simulation is not real time or demand. Closing a station is not closing a line section.
limitations: An OSM relation does not prove an operating service on a given date.
Straight edges; no accessibility or transfer width.
Two official transfers absent; Noviciado unverified; station merging is an inference.
Metro de Madrid only (no Metro Ligero, Cercanías or bus).
Planned v0.5 times are not measured; CRTM-derived timing data are not distributed.

outcomes.statement: Under the fixed rule the pilot does not proceed to the pedestrian-counter phase: with 2D footprints the isovist adds little beyond what the footprints already say. The source states that this does not mean visibility has no value.
outcomes.claim_ceiling: A geometric description, not field-validated visibility and not a walkability index. No population inference (the nine observers were placed by hand) and no pedestrian outcome was tested. Results outside the official central area are not comparable.
limitations: No heights, facades, trees or street furniture: real street visibility is lower.
Controls and isovists derive from the same footprints.
Residuals show spatial clustering (Moran's I 0.24 to 0.38).

outcomes.verdict_label: NO-GO for the production viewer at this time
outcomes.statement: The real-data run shows the rasters are technically usable (full coverage, aligned, plausible, byte-identical on rerun), which settles feasibility only. Integration into the Lens viewer is NO-GO; the research line is kept (MODIFY), to be revisited when IGN v2 or normalised building models are published and an independent check validates a height indicator.
outcomes.claim_ceiling: A feasibility demonstration, not a scientific validation; it must not be quoted as validated. MDS − MDT is not building height. No Lens question is answered by surface height.
limitations: One sheet and one barrio.
Provisional v1 models; building and vegetation not separated.
Month-level epoch (March–May 2024), spring phenology.
No independent reference compared.

outcomes.statement: The exploratory Stage 2 evaluation of agent behaviour over the unchanged MCP v0.4 recorded 0 critical errors and 1 unsupported local claim in 12 runs, which the pre-registered rule maps to MODIFY under the adopted interpretation. The result is provisional.
outcomes.claim_ceiling: Not scientific validation, not a safety claim and not evidence of improvement over earlier versions. Behaviour is not attributed to the MCP (single arm), and the adjudication was made by a language model, not an independent human.
limitations: Six cases × two repetitions, adversarial prompts; repetitions are not independent.
Classifications of three runs and the E1 sensitivity were made after seeing the results.
Stage 1 results cited elsewhere do not exist in the repository and were not verified.

figures.caption: Study design and constraint-first screening architecture. (a) The Prado–Retiro–Atocha pilot study area (≈3.5 km²) with the 27 curated tourism assets, outdoor (14) and indoor (13); a bounded pilot, not city-wide Madrid. (b) Two thermal representations feed one ordered, constraint-first gate chain; thermal state, decision confidence, evidence confidence and exclusion reason are kept separate, with no composite score.
figures.alt: Two-panel figure. Left: rectangular study-area map with 14 outdoor assets as triangles and 13 indoor assets as circles, a 500 m scale bar and a north arrow. Right: flow diagram from 27 assets through a simple proxy and a physically based SOLWEIG model into a constraint-first screen ending in either surviving alternatives or no defensible alternative.
figures.credit: Karahrodi, S. (2026), preprint v1.0, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22707470, CC BY 4.0. Asset locations © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL 1.0). Page 24 of the deposited PDF, converted to WebP.

figures.caption: Thermal-method choice changes feasibility classifications, in both directions. Of 42 outdoor asset × timestamp observations, 14 (33.3 %) were reclassified — 9 more restrictive and 5 less restrictive under the physical model; 28 agree. Neither method is field-validated.
figures.alt: Two-panel chart. Left: agreement matrix of 14 outdoor assets by three timestamps, coloured by agreement, physical-more-restrictive or physical-less-restrictive. Right: stacked bars per timestamp showing 64.3 % changed at 12:00, 0.0 % at 15:00 and 35.7 % at 18:00.
figures.credit: Karahrodi, S. (2026), preprint v1.0, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22707470, CC BY 4.0. Page 25 of the deposited PDF, converted to WebP.

figures.caption: Heat-aware screening changes the option set relative to a conventional nearest-open baseline across eight pre-registered scenarios: the candidate set changed in 7 of 8, the nearest-open pick was removed in 3 of 8, and S8 resolves to no defensible alternative — an architectural outcome of the locked constraints, not a ranked recommendation.
figures.alt: Table-like chart of eight scenarios S1 to S8 with the nearest-open baseline pick, whether it passes screening, a bar of surviving alternatives from 0 to 9, and the number removed; S8 Parque del Retiro is outlined with 0 of 26 surviving.
figures.credit: Karahrodi, S. (2026), preprint v1.0, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22707470, CC BY 4.0. Page 26 of the deposited PDF, converted to WebP.

figures.caption: Decision robustness under tested uncertainty. A satellite-derived irradiance realization changed 1 of 42 outdoor decisions; −10 % and −20 % irradiance perturbations changed none. Decision-confidence classes: ROBUST 35, BOUNDARY 6, UNSTABLE 1. Robustness covers only the tested dimensions; it is not total uncertainty and not a validation of the modelled field.
figures.alt: Two bar charts. Left: decisions changed under three solar-forcing realizations — 1 of 42, 0 of 42 and 0 of 42. Right: decision-confidence distribution — 35 robust, 6 boundary, 1 unstable, with the unstable case annotated at the 46 °C boundary.
figures.credit: Karahrodi, S. (2026), preprint v1.0, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22707470, CC BY 4.0. Page 27 of the deposited PDF, converted to WebP.

figures.caption: Straight-line versus pedestrian-network distance to the nearest municipal basic sports facility, barrio 113 San Isidro (2,636 portals). (a) Network against straight-line distance for the same origin and facility. (b) Cumulative detour ratio under the seven extraction variants. (c) Share of straight-line-inside origins that fall outside by network at 300, 500 and 800 m. A single-barrio result, not a Madrid figure.
figures.alt: Three panels. Left: scatter of network distance against straight-line distance with a 1:1 reference line, all points above it. Centre: cumulative curves of detour ratio for seven variants, one strict-pedestrian variant clearly shifted right. Right: grouped bars of false-inclusion percentages at 300, 500 and 800 m thresholds for each variant.
